summary: A wounded, unmounted hero applies a stethoscope to themself while trapped. C insight.c:ustatusline appends the injured-leg clause when Wounded_legs is true, then appends ", trapped" when u.utrap is nonzero. JavaScript currently refuses the injured-leg condition in UNPORTED_USTATUS_CONDITIONS and has a second refusal for u.utrap, so the status report never reaches its message. The selected divergence fix implements those two source branches in the existing ustatusline function.

source.branch: In insight.c:ustatusline, Wounded_legs is true, the hero is not riding, and u.utrap is nonzero. The wounded-leg report masks EWounded_legs with BOTH_SIDES, pluralizes body_part(LEG) only when both side bits are set, and emits the trapped clause after it.

evidence: Saved queue entry from accepted evaluation challenges/evaluations/accepted-41f0b9fdd4e3a7743344ba85f44b57f987d501d7-v58.json: the case has 277/306 screens, 3052/3053 RNG calls, and 277/306 cursors matched; first stop is step 277 with “the attributes window requires the injured-leg clause.” Manifest SHA256 a6846dbf74b245f8dfb0e79bbbc28a245d4bfabdf8be2f68f891da4b51b28acf and recording SHA256 bbc217ec11b0494eb25f09b8f1749d772c522a3b44488e52c093cf40f69553bf match the saved queue.

Upstream insight.c:3401-3489 defines the exact message order. Lines 3431-3440 append “, injured <leg(s)>” for Wounded_legs && !u.usteed, using EWounded_legs & BOTH_SIDES and makeplural(body_part(LEG)); line 3448 appends “, trapped” when u.utrap is set.

Current js/insight.js:ustatusline first throws for WOUNDED_LEGS in UNPORTED_USTATUS_CONDITIONS and later throws when u.utrap is set. The active command path is apply.c:use_stethoscope -> ustatusline; JS apply.js calls the corresponding insight.js function. Existing body_part and makeplural implementations are reused.
